research_findings.source: Qingzhou Luo, Farah Hariri, Lamyaa Eloussi, Darko Marinov, 'An Empirical Analysis of Flaky Tests,' FSE 2014; author-hosted conference PDF.
research_findings.locator: https://mir.cs.illinois.edu/lamyaa/publications/fse14.pdf ; web lines study-source-heda98a6ba1e59c87 L354-L370, L387-L411 and L414-L425.
research_findings.status: Published FSE 2014 paper; accessible full paper PDF hosted by author/institution.
research_findings.support: Among 161 studied commits fixing flaky tests, 74 (45%) were classified Async Wait; paper defines this as proceeding before an asynchronous call's result is available and explains missing synchronization can affect the program under test as well as a test. It separately classifies concurrency and points out nondeterministic behavior can be legitimate while a test may incorrectly reject some valid outcomes.
research_findings.applicability_and_limits: Supports keeping missing wait/order as a candidate for R04-R06 and separating test synchronization defects from product defects. This is a selected set of historical flaky-test fix commits, not a prior probability for these three reports or this C++/JavaScript project; cohort and framework transfer is limited.
research_findings.decision_use: Keep an async-order hypothesis live, but do not route all three reports to thread-race debugging. First identify whether divergence is already in normalized/shared state, appears at render, or follows a transport/poll boundary.
research_findings.discriminator: Use one captured incident event trace and matched input/configuration; place controlled gates at the suspected event boundary and compare snapshots before/after each layer. If no controlled gate exists, capture the earliest divergence at each boundary before repeating runs.

research_findings.source: Zhen Dong, Abhishek Tiwari, Xiao Liang Yu, Abhik Roychoudhury, 'Flaky Test Detection in Android via Event Order Exploration,' ESEC/FSE 2021; author-hosted full conference PDF and conference proceedings listing.
research_findings.locator: https://abhikrc.com/pdf/FSE21.pdf ; https://2021.esec-fse.org/details/fse-2021-papers/53/Flaky-Test-Detection-in-Android-via-Event-Order-Exploration ; PDF lines study-source-h843b57cbe2323d9f L84-L117, L118-L152, L290-L300, L403-L409, L495-L500, L802-L817.
research_findings.status: Published ESEC/FSE 2021 paper; accessible full conference PDF and conference program page.
research_findings.support: The paper says blind reruns may miss concurrency flakiness when the environment does not produce the needed order and noise does not guarantee different event orders. FlakeScanner traces events, maps test statements, identifies feasible schedule spaces for asynchronous events and systematically changes their positions. It reports 45/52 known Android flaky tests detected and average detection within three runs. It also reports constraints: Android event-loop assumptions, specific debug/runtime control, its class is concurrency/synchronization-related flakiness, and extra debug workload may affect failures, which authors check against debug-mode baselines.
research_findings.applicability_and_limits: Use as methodological support for controlled event-order discrimination versus unstructured reruns, not as a compatible tool or performance estimate for these excerpts. The project excerpt's shared C++ GUI, native worker and browser promise/transport are not Android; no shown scheduler hooks or equivalent event model. A controlled trace tests chosen schedules only and cannot rule out environment, rendering, protocol or unmodeled schedule causes.
research_findings.decision_use: For R04 compare identical normalized adapter events while controlling callback order; for R05 hold/resume worker progress around cancellation and replacement; for R06 defer/reject send and advance virtual timers. Prefer one minimal schedule that changes a boundary relevant to the symptom over broad repeated runs. Keep repeated runs only as a later check for residual environmental/nondeterministic behavior.
research_findings.discriminator: Record adapter/browser identity, input, config, event timestamps/order, task generation before and after each operation, and snapshots at normalization, shared state, render and transport boundaries. Force just the suspected completion/poll/event before versus after the competing action; assess whether the first divergent boundary follows that schedule.

research_findings.source: Xiaobao Cai et al., 'Reproducing Timing-Dependent GUI Flaky Tests in Android Apps via a Single Event Delay,' ISSTA 2024 technical-paper proceedings abstract.
research_findings.status: Conference program/abstract for published ISSTA 2024 paper; full text not opened in this budget.
research_findings.support: Abstract reports a focused event-delay method using failure stack traces and dynamic analysis to delay only relevant events; evaluated on 80 timing-dependent flaky tests from 22 Android apps, reproducing 73 in an average 1.71 runs and consistently over 20 runs.
research_findings.applicability_and_limits: Abstract-only, Android-specific, timing-dependent flake subset, and uses inputs (stack traces) unavailable here. Do not transfer the rates or claim feasibility for this project. It is corroborating support that schedule-targeted control can be cheaper than indiscriminate reruns when a concrete race is already localized.
research_findings.decision_use: Do not pursue event perturbation until one trace or first-divergence boundary localizes a candidate interaction; then perturb only that event pair.
research_findings.discriminator: Capture a failure trace and source boundary first; compare one targeted delayed/reordered event with the baseline trace while preserving the same adapter/browser, input and generation identity.

research_findings.source: 'An Empirical Analysis of UI-based Flaky Tests,' arXiv:2103.02669.
research_findings.locator: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.02669 ; web lines study-source-hf635c4d412ff2002 L3-L19, L34-L47, L162-L168, L655-L667.
research_findings.status: Accessible arXiv preprint; peer-reviewed publication venue/status not established by the opened source.
research_findings.support: Study analyzes 235 reported flaky UI test samples across 62 web/Android projects; reports asynchronous wait, environment, test-runner APIs, and test-script logic as cause groups, and reports timing/rendering/animation-specific categories. Its discussion states it found no strong correlation among manifestation, root cause and fix strategy groups.
research_findings.applicability_and_limits: UI-oriented corroboration for considering async wait, render timing, environment and test harness separately. Sample is issue/commit-selected and cross-platform; arXiv-only publication status is unresolved. No symptom-to-cause inference is justified from this dataset.
research_findings.decision_use: A status/list mismatch or stale view cannot by itself identify normalization, shared state, render, task scheduling or transport as cause. Instrument/check these layer boundaries independently.
research_findings.discriminator: At one exact user trace, compare normalized event, authoritative app snapshot, rendered/consumer snapshot and transport message/response; record the earliest mismatch and preserve actual adapter/browser/task identities.

research_findings.source: Lorenzo Gomez, Iulian Neamtiu, Tanzirul Azim, Todd Millstein, 'RERAN: Timing- and Touch-Sensitive Record and Replay for Android,' ICSE 2013; author-hosted conference PDF.
research_findings.locator: https://web.cs.ucla.edu/~todd/research/icse13.pdf ; web lines study-source-h68e5d9a1fdad4151 L48-L65 and L76-L85.
research_findings.status: Published ICSE 2013 conference paper; accessible full paper PDF.
research_findings.support: Paper motivates low-level recording and timed replay because high-level GUI actions can lose gesture detail, external sensor inputs and event timing; it reports successful replay across a large Android app sample and bug reproduction examples.
research_findings.applicability_and_limits: Supports preserving a concrete input/timing trace and its environment as a reproducibility artifact. Replay holds an observed input stream/timing roughly fixed; it does not by itself explore internal worker schedules, validate transport state, or distinguish whether this code rendered/published an update. Android-specific tool is not asserted compatible here.
research_findings.decision_use: Capture the exact incident inputs and event timing before changing any run conditions. Use replay to establish a matched baseline; use separate event control to test competing orders.
research_findings.discriminator: Replay a recorded trace unchanged and then vary only the suspected completion/event ordering; compare boundary snapshots and identifiers.

controlled_trace_vs_repetition.conclusion: For a first causal discriminator, capture one exact user/event/transport trace and apply one controlled event-order change at a source-supported boundary. Repetition under uncontrolled scheduling is a weak first discriminator because it neither guarantees an alternative order nor identifies the divergent layer. A deterministic trace alone can miss unrecorded environment/input sources; a controlled schedule samples only the chosen order(s). If symptoms remain intermittent or no causal schedule reproduces, perform a bounded repeat under the same captured configuration and retain all failures, passes and traces; do not treat a finite clean series as proof of absence.
layer_separation: Normalization: record raw adapter event and normalized event accepted/rejected by Application::handle (R04:74-87).
Shared state: capture app/model snapshot after state transition (R04:91-125 and test snapshot checks); establish whether mismatch exists before any rendering.

Rendering/presentation: obtain actual adapter/backend consumer and compare its visible snapshot to the authoritative shared snapshot; missing from assigned excerpts, so this remains a required evidence gap.

Task generation: retain start/cancel/replacement generation values through worker publication and UI consumption; native source guards publication but does not show the final consumer path (R05:12-35,41-58).

Transport: retain browser/client identity, poll request/settlement/error, failure flags, task/correlation generation if present, and consumer state. R06 excerpt shows poll lifecycle only, not response decoding or rendering.
controlled_trace_vs_repetition.identity_rule: Do not replace missing identifiers with guesses. R04 incident adapter and R06 browser/transport are unknown. R05 native versus cooperative executor is unknown. R06 has no generation value in the shown lifecycle module; record it as unavailable until caller/client code is inspected.
controlled_trace_vs_repetition.no_causal_merge: The three hypothetical symptoms are independent reports; shared GUI ancestry or similar timing language does not establish a common cause.
